question:
A set of jobs `Jobs` need to be processed on a set of machines `Machines` in series. All jobs have the same processing order through all the machines from machine 1 to machine M. Each machine can work in parallel. The workflow is the following: the first job of the sequence goes to the first machine to be processed; meanwhile, other jobs wait; when the first machine has processed the first job, the first job goes to the second machine and the second job of the sequence starts to be processed by the first machine; and so on. The time required to process job `j` on machine `m` is `ProcesTime_{j, m}`. The problem aims to minimize the total makespan. The goal is to find a sequence of jobs that minimize the makespan: the time when all jobs have been processed.

The following parameters are included in this problem:
jobs: list of ints, represents a set of all Jobs
schedules: list of ints, represents a set of all schedules, range [1, S]
machines: list of ints, represents a set of all machines, range [1, M]
proces_time: 2D list of ints, time required to process job `j` on machine `m`, domain size [Jobs x Machines]


The following data is included in this problem:
{'jobs': [1, 2, 3], 'schedules': [1, 2, 3], 'machines': [1, 2], 'proces_time': [[1, 3], [2, 2], [3, 1]]}

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "jobs": [1, 2, 3],
    "schedules": [1, 2, 3],
    "machines": [1, 2],
    "proces_time": [[1, 3], [2, 2], [3, 1]],  # proces_time[j-1][m-1]
    "big_M": 1000,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    jobs = d["jobs"]
    schedules = d["schedules"]
    machines = d["machines"]
    p = d["proces_time"]
    big_m = d["big_M"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.Jobs = pyo.Set(initialize=jobs)
    model.Schedules = pyo.Set(initialize=schedules)
    model.Machines = pyo.Set(initialize=machines)

    # processing time lookup: ptime[j, m]
    ptime = {(j, m): p[j - 1][m - 1] for j in jobs for m in machines}

    # --- Variables ---
    model.assign = pyo.Var(model.Jobs, model.Schedules, within=pyo.Binary)
    model.start = pyo.Var(model.Jobs, model.Machines, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    model.makespan = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # --- Objective ---
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.makespan, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # --- Constraints ---

    # Each job assigned to exactly one sequence position
    def job_once_rule(m, j):
        return sum(m.assign[j, s] for s in m.Schedules) == 1

    model.job_once = pyo.Constraint(model.Jobs, rule=job_once_rule)

    # Each sequence position holds exactly one job
    def slot_once_rule(m, s):
        return sum(m.assign[j, s] for j in m.Jobs) == 1

    model.slot_once = pyo.Constraint(model.Schedules, rule=slot_once_rule)

    # Precedence within a job across consecutive machines (flow shop order)
    def precedence_rule(m, j, m_idx):
        m_list = list(m.Machines)
        if m_idx == m_list[0]:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        prev_m = m_list[m_list.index(m_idx) - 1]
        return m.start[j, m_idx] >= m.start[j, prev_m] + ptime[j, prev_m]

    model.precedence = pyo.Constraint(
        model.Jobs, model.Machines, rule=precedence_rule
    )

    # Machine capacity: jobs run in sequence-position order on each machine.
    # Linear big-M form: for each machine m, position s (s>1), and pair (j1 at prev_s, j2 at s):
    # start[j2,m] >= start[j1,m] + ptime[j1,m] - M*(2 - assign[j1,prev_s] - assign[j2,s])
    def machine_order_rule(m, m_idx, s, j1, j2):
        s_list = list(m.Schedules)
        if s == s_list[0]:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        prev_s = s_list[s_list.index(s) - 1]
        return m.start[j2, m_idx] >= (
            m.start[j1, m_idx]
            + ptime[j1, m_idx]
            - big_m * (2 - m.assign[j1, prev_s] - m.assign[j2, s])
        )

    model.machine_order = pyo.Constraint(
        model.Machines,
        model.Schedules,
        model.Jobs,
        model.Jobs,
        rule=machine_order_rule,
    )

    # Makespan: at least the completion time of every job on the last machine
    last_machine = list(machines)[-1]

    def makespan_rule(m, j):
        return m.makespan >= m.start[j, last_machine] + ptime[j, last_machine]

    model.makespan_def = pyo.Constraint(model.Jobs, rule=makespan_rule)

    return model

def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    jobs = d["jobs"]
    machines = d["machines"]
    p_time = d["proces_time"]
    bigM = d["bigM"]

    def proc(j, m):
        # 1-based job/machine -> 0-based list index
        return p_time[j - 1][m - 1]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- Sets
    model.Jobs = pyo.Set(initialize=jobs, ordered=True)
    model.Machines = pyo.Set(initialize=machines, ordered=True)
    # ordered disjoint pairs of jobs, used for the disjunctive constraints
    pairs = [(j, k) for j in jobs for k in jobs if j < k]
    model.Pairs = pyo.Set(initialize=pairs, dimen=2)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------- Variables
    model.s = pyo.Var(
        model.Jobs, model.Machines,
        domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, None)
    )
    model.Cmax = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=(0, None))
    model.y = pyo.Var(
        model.Pairs, model.Machines,
        domain=pyo.Binary
    )

    # --------------------------------------------------------- Objective
    # Minimise the total makespan
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.Cmax, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # ------------------------------------------------------- Constraints

    # Within a job, machine m+1 starts after machine m finishes (series order).
    def precedence_rule(b, j, m):
        nxt = m + 1
        if nxt in machines:
            return b.s[j, nxt] >= b.s[j, m] + proc(j, m)
        return pyo.Constraint.Skip

    model.precedence = pyo.Constraint(
        model.Jobs, model.Machines, rule=precedence_rule
    )

    # Disjunctive: on each machine jobs must not overlap.
    # y[j,k,m] = 1 means job j runs before job k on machine m.
    def machine_order_rule(b, j, k, m):
        return (b.s[k, m] >= b.s[j, m] + proc(j, m) - bigM * (1 - b.y[j, k, m]))

    model.order_forward = pyo.Constraint(
        model.Pairs, model.Machines, rule=machine_order_rule
    )

    def machine_order_rule_rev(b, j, k, m):
        return (b.s[j, m] >= b.s[k, m] + proc(k, m) - bigM * b.y[j, k, m])

    model.order_backward = pyo.Constraint(
        model.Pairs, model.Machines, rule=machine_order_rule_rev
    )

    # Makespan >= completion time of every job on its last machine.
    last_machine = max(machines)

    def makespan_rule(b, j):
        return b.Cmax >= b.s[j, last_machine] + proc(j, last_machine)

    model.makespan_def = pyo.Constraint(model.Jobs, rule=makespan_rule)

    return model

DATA = {
    "jobs": [1, 2, 3],
    "schedules": [1, 2, 3],
    "machines": [1, 2],
    "proces_time": [[1, 3], [2, 2], [3, 1]],  # proces_time[j-1][m-1]

}


def build_model(data=None):

    jobs = d["jobs"]
    schedules = d["schedules"]
    machines = d["machines"]
    p = d["proces_time"]  # p[j-1][m-1] : job j on machine m
    big_M = d["big_M"]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # MODEL
    # ------------------------------------------------------------

    # ---------------- Sets ----------------
    model.J = pyo.Set(initialize=jobs, ordered=True)        # jobs
    model.S = pyo.Set(initialize=schedules, ordered=True)   # sequence positions
    model.M = pyo.Set(initialize=machines, ordered=True)    # machines

    # Predecessor sets (avoid python max/min on pyomo expressions)
    model.S_prev = pyo.Set(
        initialize=[(s, t) for s in schedules for t in schedules if t < s],
        dimen=2,
    )
    model.M_prev = pyo.Set(
        initialize=[(k, l) for k in machines for l in machines if l < k],
        dimen=2,
    )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # Parameters (PROC[j,m] = time of real job j on machine m)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    model.PROC = pyo.Param(
        model.J, model.M, initialize=lambda m, j, k: p[j - 1][k - 1]
    )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # VARIABLES
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # x[s,j] = 1 if real job j is placed at sequence position s
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.S, model.J, domain=pyo.Binary)

    # start[s,k] = start time of the job placed at position s on machine k
    model.start = pyo.Var(model.S, model.M, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # makespan
    model.Cmax = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # CONSTRAINTS
    # ------------------------------------------------------------

    # 1) Each position of the sequence gets exactly one real job.
    def rule_one_job_per_position(m, s):
        return sum(m.x[s, j] for j in m.J) == 1
    model.one_job_per_position = pyo.Constraint(
        model.S, rule=rule_one_job_per_position
    )

    # 2) Each real job fills exactly one position.
    def rule_one_position_per_job(m, j):
        return sum(m.x[s, j] for s in m.S) == 1
    model.one_position_per_job = pyo.Constraint(
        model.J, rule=rule_one_position_per_job
    )

    # 3) First job of the sequence starts on machine 1 at time 0.
    def rule_first_start(m):
        return m.start[1, 1] == 0
    model.first_start = pyo.Constraint(rule=rule_first_start)

    # 4) Sequence chain on machine 1: start[s,1] >= start[t,1] + proc time
    #    of the job placed at position t (t is the predecessor of s).
    def rule_seq_machine1(m, s, t):
        proc_prev = sum(m.PROC[j, 1] * m.x[t, j] for j in m.J)
        return m.start[s, 1] >= m.start[t, 1] + proc_prev
    model.seq_machine1 = pyo.Constraint(
        model.S_prev, rule=rule_seq_machine1
    )

    # 5) Within a job, machine k starts after it finished on machine l
    #    (l is the predecessor machine of k).
    def rule_machine_order(m, s, k, l):
        proc_l = sum(m.PROC[j, l] * m.x[s, j] for j in m.J)
        return m.start[s, k] >= m.start[s, l] + proc_l
    model.machine_order = pyo.Constraint(
        model.S, model.M_prev, rule=rule_machine_order
    )

    # 6) Same machine works on jobs one at a time in sequence order.
    def rule_machine_capacity(m, s, t, k):
        proc_t_k = sum(m.PROC[j, k] * m.x[t, j] for j in m.J)
        return m.start[s, k] >= m.start[t, k] + proc_t_k
    model.machine_capacity = pyo.Constraint(
        model.S_prev, model.M, rule=rule_machine_capacity
    )

    # 7) Makespan: every position's job must finish its last machine.
    def rule_makespan(m, s, k):
        proc = sum(m.PROC[j, k] * m.x[s, j] for j in m.J)
        return m.Cmax >= m.start[s, k] + proc
    model.link_makespan = pyo.Constraint(
        model.S, model.M, rule=rule_makespan
    )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    # OBJECTIVE : minimize the total makespan
    # ------------------------------------------------------------
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.Cmax, sense=pyo.minimize)

    return model

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Structured formulation summary
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PROBLEM: Flow-shop scheduling. All jobs visit machines 1..M in the same
# order. Each machine processes one job at a time. Find the job sequence that
# minimizes the makespan (completion time of the last job on the last machine).
#
# SETS / INDICES
#   Jobs     : jobs to schedule                       -> DATA["jobs"]
#   Machines : machines in fixed order 1..M           -> DATA["machines"]
#   Schedules: positions in the sequence 1..S         -> DATA["schedules"]
#   (S == number of jobs; each position holds exactly one job)
#
# DECISION VARIABLES
#   x[j, k]   Binary          : 1 if job j is placed at sequence position k
#   s[j, m]   NonNegativeReals: start time of job j on machine m
#   Cmax      NonNegativeReals: makespan (finish of last operation)
#
# OBJECTIVE (minimize)
#   Minimize Cmax : the time when all jobs have been processed.
#
# CONSTRAINTS
#   1) Assignment: each job occupies exactly one position.
#   2) Assignment: each position holds exactly one job.
#   3) Precedence within a job: job j on machine m+1 starts after it finishes
#      on machine m (same job, consecutive machines).
#   4) Machine capacity / no overlap: for two jobs occupying consecutive
#      sequence positions k and k+1, the job at position k+1 cannot start on
#      machine m until the job at position k has finished on machine m.
#      (Permutation flow-shop: sequence order is the same on every machine.)
#   5) Makespan: Cmax >= finish time of the job in the last position on the
#      last machine.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

DATA = {
    "jobs": [1, 2, 3],
    "schedules": [1, 2, 3],
    "machines": [1, 2],
    "proces_time": [[1, 3], [2, 2], [3, 1]],
    "big_M": 10000,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    jobs = list(d["jobs"])
    machines = list(d["machines"])
    schedules = list(d["schedules"])
    p = d["proces_time"]
    bigM = d["big_M"]

    # processing time lookup: ptime[j][m]
    ptime = {j: {m: p[j - 1][m - 1] for m in machines} for j in jobs}

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.Jobs = pyo.Set(initialize=jobs)
    model.Machines = pyo.Set(initialize=machines)
    model.Schedules = pyo.Set(initialize=schedules)

    # x[j, k] = 1 if job j is at sequence position k
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.Jobs, model.Schedules, within=pyo.Binary)

    # start time of job j on machine m
    model.s = pyo.Var(model.Jobs, model.Machines, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # makespan
    model.Cmax = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # ---- Constraint 1: each job occupies exactly one position -------------
    def job_assignment_rule(m, j):
        return sum(m.x[j, k] for k in m.Schedules) == 1

    model.job_assignment = pyo.Constraint(model.Jobs, rule=job_assignment_rule)

    # ---- Constraint 2: each position holds exactly one job ----------------
    def position_assignment_rule(m, k):
        return sum(m.x[j, k] for j in m.Jobs) == 1

    model.position_assignment = pyo.Constraint(
        model.Schedules, rule=position_assignment_rule
    )

    # ---- Constraint 3: precedence within a job across machines ------------
    # s[j, m+1] >= s[j, m] + ptime[j][m]
    machine_pairs = [
        (machines[i], machines[i + 1]) for i in range(len(machines) - 1)
    ]

    def job_precedence_rule(m, j, m1, m2):
        return m.s[j, m2] >= m.s[j, m1] + ptime[j][m1]

    model.job_precedence = pyo.Constraint(
        model.Jobs, machine_pairs, rule=job_precedence_rule
    )

    # ---- Constraint 4: machine capacity (no overlap) ----------------------
    # For consecutive positions k, k+1 and machine m:
    #   s[j2, m] >= s[j1, m] + ptime[j1][m] - bigM*(2 - x[j1,k] - x[j2,k+1])
    # where j1 is the job at position k and j2 the job at position k+1.
    position_pairs = [
        (schedules[i], schedules[i + 1]) for i in range(len(schedules) - 1)
    ]

    def machine_capacity_rule(m, j1, j2, k1, k2, mach):
        return m.s[j2, mach] >= (
            m.s[j1, mach]
            + ptime[j1][mach]
            - bigM * (2 - m.x[j1, k1] - m.x[j2, k2])
        )

    model.machine_capacity = pyo.Constraint(
        model.Jobs,
        model.Jobs,
        position_pairs,
        model.Machines,
        rule=machine_capacity_rule,
    )

    # ---- Constraint 5: makespan -------------------------------------------
    last_machine = machines[-1]
    last_position = schedules[-1]

    def makespan_rule(m, j):
        return m.Cmax >= (
            m.s[j, last_machine]
            + ptime[j][last_machine]
            - bigM * (1 - m.x[j, last_position])
        )

    model.makespan = pyo.Constraint(model.Jobs, rule=makespan_rule)

    # ---- Objective --------------------------------------------------------
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.Cmax, sense=pyo.minimize)

    return model

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Problem: Permutation Flow Shop Scheduling (minimize makespan)
#
# Sets / indices
#   Jobs      = {1,2,3}          jobs to be processed
#   Schedules = {1,2,3}          positions in the processing sequence
#   Machines  = {1,2}            machines, processed in order 1..M
#
# Decision variables
#   x[j, s]      in {0,1}        job j is placed at sequence position s
#   start[s, m]  >= 0            start time of the job at position s on machine m
#   Cmax         >= 0            makespan (completion of last job on last machine)
#
# Objective (minimize)
#   minimize Cmax
#
# Constraints
#   (1) Each position holds exactly one job.            sum_j x[j,s] = 1
#   (2) Each job occupies exactly one position.         sum_s x[j,s] = 1
#   (3) Machine precedence within a job (position s):
#       start[s,m] >= start[s,m-1] + processing time of the job at s on m-1
#       -> linearised with big-M using x[j,s].
#   (4) No overlap on a machine between consecutive positions:
#       start[s,m] >= start[s-1,m] + processing time of the job at s-1 on m
#       -> linearised with big-M using x[j,s-1].
#   (5) Makespan definition: Cmax >= start[s,M] + processing time of job at s on M.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

DATA = {
    "jobs": [1, 2, 3],
    "schedules": [1, 2, 3],
    "machines": [1, 2],
    "proces_time": [[1, 3], [2, 2], [3, 1]],
    "bigM": 1000,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    jobs = list(d["jobs"])
    schedules = list(d["schedules"])
    machines = list(d["machines"])
    p = d["proces_time"]
    M = d["bigM"]

    # processing time lookup: ptime[j][m]
    ptime = {j: {m: p[j - 1][m - 1] for m in machines} for j in jobs}

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.Jobs = pyo.Set(initialize=jobs)
    model.Schedules = pyo.Set(initialize=schedules)
    model.Machines = pyo.Set(initialize=machines)

    # x[j,s] = 1 if job j is at sequence position s
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.Jobs, model.Schedules, within=pyo.Binary)

    # start[s,m] = start time of the job at position s on machine m
    model.start = pyo.Var(model.Schedules, model.Machines, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # makespan
    model.Cmax = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # (1) each position holds exactly one job
    def rule_pos_assign(m, s):
        return sum(m.x[j, s] for j in m.Jobs) == 1
    model.pos_assign = pyo.Constraint(model.Schedules, rule=rule_pos_assign)

    # (2) each job occupies exactly one position
    def rule_job_assign(m, j):
        return sum(m.x[j, s] for s in m.Schedules) == 1
    model.job_assign = pyo.Constraint(model.Jobs, rule=rule_job_assign)

        proc = sum(ptime[j][prev] * m.x[j, s] for j in m.Jobs)
        return m.start[s, mm] >= m.start[s, prev] + proc
    model.machine_prec = pyo.Constraint(
        model.Schedules, model.Machines, rule=rule_machine_prec

    #     start[s,m] >= start[s-1,m] + p(job at s-1, m)
    def rule_machine_nooverlap(m, s, mm):
        if s == m.Schedules.first():
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        prev_s = s - 1
        proc = sum(ptime[j][mm] * m.x[j, prev_s] for j in m.Jobs)
        return m.start[s, mm] >= m.start[prev_s, mm] + proc
    model.machine_nooverlap = pyo.Constraint(
        model.Schedules, model.Machines, rule=rule_machine_nooverlap
    )

    # (5) makespan definition
    last_m = max(machines)

    def rule_makespan(m, s):
        proc = sum(ptime[j][last_m] * m.x[j, s] for j in m.Jobs)
        return m.Cmax >= m.start[s, last_m] + proc
    model.makespan_def = pyo.Constraint(model.Schedules, rule=rule_makespan)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.Cmax, sense=pyo.minimize)

        model.Jobs, rule=one_position_per_job_rule
    )

    def before_link_rule(m, j, k):
        pos_j = sum(s * m.assign[j, s] for s in m.Schedules)

        model.JobPairs, rule=before_link_rev_rule

def build_model(data=None):

    schedules = d["schedules"]
    machines = d["machines"]
    p = d["proces_time"]
    bigM = d["bigM"]

    # helper: processing time of job j on machine m  (1-indexed)
    def ptime(j, m):
        return p[j - 1][m - 1]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ Sets
    model.J = pyo.Set(initialize=jobs, ordered=True)        # jobs
    model.S = pyo.Set(initialize=schedules, ordered=True)   # sequence positions
    model.M = pyo.Set(initialize=machines, ordered=True)    # machines

    # --------------------------------------------------------------- Vars
    # x[j,s] = 1 if job j is scheduled in sequence position s
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.J, model.S, within=pyo.Binary)

    # C[s,m] = completion time of the job in position s on machine m
    model.C = pyo.Var(model.S, model.M, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # makespan
    model.Cmax = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------- Objective
    # "minimize the total makespan"
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.Cmax, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # --------------------------------------------------------- Constraints
    # Each job occupies exactly one sequence position.
    def job_assign_rule(m, j):
        return sum(m.x[j, s] for s in m.S) == 1
    model.job_assign = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=job_assign_rule)

    # Each sequence position holds exactly one job.
    def pos_assign_rule(m, s):
        return sum(m.x[j, s] for j in m.J) == 1
    model.pos_assign = pyo.Constraint(model.S, rule=pos_assign_rule)

    # For the FIRST position, there is no preceding position: machine m can only
    # start after machine m-1 finishes for the same (only) job.
    first_s = schedules[0]
    first_m = machines[0]

        # machine 1 completion for position s >= completion of previous pos on m1 + p
        if s == first_s:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        return m.C[s, first_m] >= m.C[s - 1, first_m] + sum(
            m.x[j, s] * ptime(j, first_m) for j in m.J
        )
    model.first_machine = pyo.Constraint(model.S, rule=first_machine_rule)

        return m.C[s, mm] >= m.C[s, mm - 1] + sum(
            m.x[j, s] * ptime(j, mm) for j in m.J

    model.later_machine_own = pyo.Constraint(
        model.S, model.M, rule=later_machine_own_rule

        return m.C[s, mm] >= m.C[s - 1, mm] + sum(

        return m.Cmax >= m.C[s, last_m]
    model.makespan = pyo.Constraint(model.S, rule=makespan_rule)
